expect: A climbing hydrangea that uses aerial roots to cling to walls and other structures, creating excellent coverage over time. Glossy green leaves provide the backdrop for lacecap flowers in summer. The white blooms are held in flat clusters above the foliage.
description: A self-clinging climber for a shady north or east wall, and the easiest of the climbing hydrangeas to tell apart in flower. Each white lacecap is ringed with single teardrop bracts rather than the four-petalled florets of a true climbing hydrangea, which gives the flower heads a lighter, more open look. Glossy heart-shaped leaves cover a wall densely once established. Often sold as Schizophragma hydrangeoides.
why: The catalog holds three near-identical white-lacecap climbers on aerial roots (Hydrangea anomala, H. petiolaris, H. hydrangeoides) and the old text described all three equally well, so a reader could not tell them apart. This species is the former Schizophragma hydrangeoides and its sterile florets are single large bracts rather than four-petalled, which is the one difference visible from a path. Ana's ruling 2026-08-17: keep it, and say what makes it different.
